title: 3.7.21 Lab: Mutating vs. Non-Mutating Methods Drill
description: Demonstrate one method that changes its array and one that returns a new array, logging before and after each. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Create a working array
steps.instructions: Create a variable that holds an array of at least three values. You will demonstrate two methods on it.

steps.title: Demonstrate a mutating method
steps.instructions: Call a method that changes the array in place, such as .push(). Log the array before and after so the change is visible.

steps.title: Demonstrate a non-mutating method
steps.instructions: Call a method that returns a new array and leaves the original alone, such as .map() or .slice(). Store the result in a new variable and log it.

steps.title: Log both results
steps.instructions: Use console.log to print the original array after the non-mutating call, so you can see it did not change.

requirements.title: Array declared
requirements.description: Makes an array in square brackets. Help: 3.7.19 (What Else Is Out There)
requirements.hint: Make an array in square brackets, in a variable or as a property of an object.

requirements.title: A mutating method is called
requirements.description: Calls .push() (or another in-place method). Help: 3.7.19 (What Else Is Out There)
requirements.hint: Call a method that changes the array in place, such as .push, then log the array to see it change.

requirements.title: A non-mutating method is called
requirements.description: Calls .map(), .slice() or .concat(), which return a new array. Help: 3.7.19 (What Else Is Out There)
requirements.hint: Call a method that returns a new array and leaves the original alone, such as .map, .slice or .concat.

requirements.title: console.log present
requirements.description: Calls console.log to show before and after. Help: 3.7.19 (What Else Is Out There)
requirements.hint: Log before and after so you can see which call changed the original.

requirements.title: before and after are printed
requirements.description: At least two different values are printed. Help: 3.7.19 (What Else Is Out There)
requirements.hint: Print the array before and after each call so you can see which method changed it and which did not.

checks.fail: Print the array before and after the calls, so the output shows which method changed it.

requirements.title: the array is printed before and after the in-place call, by code that runs
requirements.description: At least three console.log calls that run print your data, and two prints of the array itself differ, before and after the method that changes it. Help: 3.7.19 (What Else Is Out There)
requirements.hint: Print the array, call the method that changes it, print the array again, then print the new array. Typed-in text does not change with the data, so it does not count.

checks.fail: Print with console.log calls that run and show your array's data: the array before the change, after it, and the new array, at least three prints. Typed-in text does not count.

Print the array (a label is fine, a copy such as [...a] too) before AND after a method that changes THAT array in place, such as a.push(...), on it, an alias or a parameter. A new array does not count.

planChart.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A([Start]) --> B[make a list of at least three values]
  B --> C[/log the list/]
  C --> D[change the list in place with a mutating method]
  D --> E[/log the list again/]
  E --> F[make a new list with a non-mutating method]
  F --> G[/log the new list and the original/]
  G --> H([End])
